hosted-agent.title: Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service – Microsoft Learn
hosted-agent.notes: Hosted agents are containerized agentic AI applications that run on Foundry Agent Service. Unlike prompt-based agents, which are defined only through prompts and tool settings in the portal, the agent's code is itself a container image, and the developer picks the framework and controls runtime behavior. Models come from the Foundry model catalog while the custom code handles orchestration. The platform takes over cross-cutting work such as containerization, web server setup, security, memory persistence, scaling, instrumentation and version rollbacks. Supported frameworks include Microsoft Agent Framework, LangChain and LangGraph, or custom code in Python and C#. Each agent gets its own Microsoft Entra identity and a dedicated endpoint, and every session runs in a VM-isolated sandbox with a persistent file system and scale-to-zero. Versions are immutable, and an endpoint serves one version at a time without traffic splitting. A container image in Azure Container Registry and a Foundry project are required, and billing follows CPU and memory use during active sessions. Secrets should not be placed in images or environment variables; managed identities and Key Vault are the recommended route.

hybrid-runbook-worker.title: Azure Automation Hybrid Runbook Worker Overview – Microsoft Learn
hybrid-runbook-worker.notes: The Hybrid Runbook Worker is an Azure Automation role that runs runbooks directly on a machine in a local datacenter or at another cloud provider. The runbooks stay stored and managed in Azure Automation and are delivered to the assigned machines. This solves the problem that runbooks running on the Azure platform may not reach resources elsewhere. The supported model is extension-based: a VM extension, handled by the Azure VM agent or the Azure Connected Machine agent for Arc-enabled servers, installs the worker and authenticates through a system-assigned managed identity. The older agent-based model has been retired. Each worker belongs to a worker group, and a group with several workers gives high availability; jobs are sent to a group, not to a specific worker. Workers poll for jobs regularly, and jobs run under the local System account on Windows or nxautomation on Linux. Typical uses are in-guest VM management, long-running or resource-heavy automation, access to private or on-premises services, and cases where data must stay local. A machine hosts only one worker, a worker reports to one Automation account, and runbooks need their own authentication, for example a managed identity.

hyper-v.title: Hyper-V virtualization in Windows Server and Windows – Microsoft Learn
hyper-v.notes: Hyper-V is Microsoft's hypervisor technology, built into Windows Server and Windows, and it runs as a type-1 hypervisor directly on the hardware. It is used to create and run virtual machines for server consolidation, better hardware use, resilience and disaster recovery. Guests can be Windows, Linux or FreeBSD systems. Generation 2 virtual machines add UEFI, Secure Boot and a virtual TPM 2.0, and shielded VMs combine BitLocker, Secure Boot and attestation, with the Host Guardian Service limiting which hosts may run them. For storage the page lists Storage Spaces Direct, Storage Spaces, iSCSI, Fibre Channel, SMB and NFS. Availability features include failover clustering with Cluster Shared Volumes and live migration, and Hyper-V Replica together with Azure Site Recovery covers disaster recovery. Management tools include Hyper-V Manager, PowerShell, PowerShell Direct, Windows Admin Center and System Center Virtual Machine Manager. Hyper-V is a role in all editions of Windows Server 2025 and is included in the Pro, Enterprise and Education editions of Windows 11, where it mainly serves local development and test needs. The page does not give concrete limits for vCPUs, memory or VM counts.

identity-threat-detection-and-response.title: Identity Threat Detection and Response (ITDR) – Microsoft Security
identity-threat-detection-and-response.notes: Identity threat detection and response, or ITDR, is described as a security focus area with solutions that prevent, detect and respond to attacks aimed at identities. The page notes that many identity attacks begin with stolen credentials, for example through phishing or social engineering, and that attackers increasingly target the identity infrastructure and weaknesses in its configuration. A central idea is that identity administrators and security operations teams should work together instead of separately. Listed capabilities include adaptive access control that evaluates risk in real time, correlation of signals from endpoints, email, collaboration tools and SaaS apps, and UEBA-based anomaly detection that can trigger step-up authentication or block access. Further functions are automated disruption of attacks and lateral movement and autonomous investigation of risky identities. Coverage extends to human and non-human identities across cloud, hybrid and on-premises environments. Microsoft Entra ID Protection and Microsoft Defender for Identity are named as the products involved, and the FAQ says the capabilities are offered through the Microsoft Defender Suite. The page does not name specific license SKUs or technical limits.

insecure-deserialization.title: Deserialization risks in use of BinaryFormatter and related types – .NET – Microsoft Learn
insecure-deserialization.notes: Deserialization vulnerabilities are a threat category in which request payloads are processed unsafely. Attackers can use them to cause denial of service, information disclosure or remote code execution in the target application, and the category appears consistently in the OWASP Top 10 across languages such as C, C++, Java and C#. In .NET the main risk comes from apps that use BinaryFormatter, because an attacker can influence control flow and run code in the context of the target process. The page compares calling BinaryFormatter.Deserialize on a payload to launching that payload as an executable. Denial of service cannot be prevented with a SerializationBinder or other settings, and a binder may not be enough to stop information disclosure or code execution either. The recommended response is to stop using BinaryFormatter, even for data believed to be trusted, and to move to XmlSerializer, DataContractSerializer or System.Text.Json. Related formatters such as SoapFormatter, LosFormatter, NetDataContractSerializer and ObjectStateFormatter are to be avoided because they also allow unrestricted polymorphic deserialization. The page stresses that serialized data crossing into or out of an app almost always crosses a trust boundary.

intrusion-detection-and-prevention-syste.title: Azure Firewall Premium features implementation guide – Microsoft Learn
intrusion-detection-and-prevention-syste.notes: A network intrusion detection and prevention system monitors a network for malicious activity, logs and reports what it finds, and can optionally block it. In Azure, this capability is a feature of the Azure Firewall Premium SKU. It is signature based: it recognizes specific patterns such as byte sequences in traffic or command sequences known from malware. The signatures cover the application and network layers, are fully managed, and are updated continuously. They apply to inbound traffic, spoke-to-spoke traffic and outbound traffic, including traffic to and from on-premises networks. Each signature can run in one of three modes: disabled, alert, or alert and deny, and the effective mode depends on the policy, a parent policy, an override or the system default. Signatures carry a severity and a traffic direction, and private IP ranges follow RFC 1918 by default and can be adjusted. A bypass list can exclude certain addresses or subnets from filtering. Alerts can be found in the network rule logs. Encrypted HTTPS traffic is only inspected in content when TLS inspection is enabled, and the number of custom IDPS rules is capped.

isolated-storage.title: Isolated Storage – Business Central – Microsoft Learn
isolated-storage.notes: Isolated storage in Business Central is a data store that keeps extensions separated from each other. An extension saves values as key-value pairs, and other extensions cannot retrieve those pairs. Access goes through an API exposed as the IsolatedStorage data type in the AL language. The available methods let an extension set a value for a key, read it back, check whether a key exists, and delete it. Each of these methods can take a data scope argument, which classifies the stored data. There is also a method that encrypts the value before storing it, and that method limits the plain-text input to a fixed number of characters, with special characters taking up more space. The page names the DataScope option type and the IsolatedStorage data type as related reference material. It states no prerequisites and gives no specific usage scenarios beyond protecting an extension's values from other extensions, and it does not describe size limits or environment handling.

log4j.title: Guidance for preventing, detecting, and hunting for exploitation of the Log4j 2 vulnerability – Microsoft Security Blog
log4j.notes: Log4j 2 is an open-source component from the Apache Foundation that is embedded in many third-party software products and services. Several vulnerabilities in it, including CVE-2021-44228, known as Log4Shell, allow remote code execution. In an attack, a specially crafted string containing the substring jndi, followed by a protocol such as ldap or rmi and an attacker-controlled domain, makes the affected process connect out and load code; attackers sometimes obfuscate the string to evade simple detection. Affected items include Log4j libraries, especially log4j-core JAR files, applications that bundle them on Windows and Linux, and container images. Observed activity covered mass scanning, coin mining, remote shells and use by ransomware operators. Recommended actions are to apply vendor patches quickly and, as a workaround, to disable JNDI lookups through the LOG4J_FORMAT_MSG_NO_LOOKUPS environment variable. For detection, the post points to vulnerability dashboards in Microsoft Defender, Defender alerts, antivirus signatures, a Microsoft Sentinel solution, container image scanning and Azure Firewall Premium with its intrusion prevention in alert-and-deny mode.

lora.title: GitHub – microsoft/LoRA: Code for loralib, an implementation of "LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models"
lora.notes: LoRA, short for low-rank adaptation, is a method for adapting large language models in which the original pretrained weights are frozen and pairs of low-rank decomposition matrices are trained instead. This greatly reduces the number of trainable parameters and the storage needed for each task-specific model, and it makes switching between tasks at deployment more efficient. According to the repository, it adds no extra inference latency. The Python package loralib implements it for PyTorch: layers are replaced with LoRA variants, only the LoRA parameters are marked as trainable, and only those parameters are saved as a small checkpoint that is loaded on top of the pretrained one. Switching the model to evaluation mode merges the LoRA weights into the base weights, and training mode reverses this. Supported layer types include linear, embedding and convolutional layers, plus a merged linear layer for combined attention projections. The examples adapt query and value projections in transformers, although LoRA can target other subsets of weights. The page reports results on RoBERTa, DeBERTa and GPT-2, notes that the best setup varies by architecture and task, and mentions support in the Hugging Face PEFT library.

managed-solution.title: Solution concepts with Power Platform – Microsoft Learn
managed-solution.notes: A Power Platform solution is either unmanaged or managed. Unmanaged solutions are used in development environments and are regarded as the source of the platform's assets; they can be exported as unmanaged or as managed, and exported unmanaged versions should be kept in source control. Deleting an unmanaged solution removes only the container, while the customizations stay active as part of the default solution. Managed solutions are meant for deployment to test, UAT, SIT and production environments, but not to the development environment where the solution was built. As an ALM practice, a managed solution is produced by exporting an unmanaged one and is treated as a build artifact. Components cannot be edited directly inside a managed solution, and changing a managed component creates a dependency that blocks uninstalling the managed solution. A managed solution cannot be exported, and it cannot be imported into the same environment that holds the original unmanaged solution, so testing needs a separate environment. Deleting a managed solution removes its customizations and can cause data loss in the custom tables and columns it contains.

mapi.title: Outlook MAPI Reference – Microsoft Learn
mapi.notes: The Microsoft Learn reference page calls MAPI the Microsoft Outlook Messaging API and says it provides the messaging architecture for Outlook 2013 and Outlook 2016. It supplies interfaces, functions and data types that developers use to build Outlook messaging applications. Applications and transports use MAPI to work with email data, to create messages and the folders that hold them, and to receive notifications when MAPI-related data changes. The reference is organized into four parts: a getting-started overview, sample applications, concept guides for understanding and programming with MAPI, and the reference for its programming elements. For newcomers the page points to a separate article on selecting the right API or technology for developing Outlook solutions. The page applies only to Outlook 2013 and Outlook 2016 and does not list individual interfaces, functions or code examples, nor does it describe further requirements or restrictions.
